Definition: remission (of debt) or suspension of labor)
BiblicalUsage: Release is the seventh year. At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release: every creditor shall release what his neighbour owes, because it is called the LORD's release. Moses warns against the evil thought that withholds from the poor brother because the year of release is at hand, and commands the law to be read in the solemnity of the year of release.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe release is the gospel in the law. Debts forgiven, slaves freed, the poor not turned away, and I hold that God releases His people so they will release one another.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
